question: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length \(2\) and an acute angle of \(30°\). What is the length of the side opposite this angle?
solution: The opposite side equals the hypotenuse multiplied by the sine of the angle: \(2\times 1/2=1\).

reference.question: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length \(2\) and an acute angle of \(30°\). What is the length of the side opposite this angle?
reference.solution:
Method 1: Sine ratio

The opposite side equals the hypotenuse multiplied by the sine of the angle: \(2\times 1/2=1\).

Method 2: Thirty-degree right-triangle property

In a right triangle, the side opposite a \(30^\circ\) angle is half the hypotenuse. The requested length is therefore \(\frac{2}{2}=1\).
